query: Why do resolution duration values vary across tickets?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Categorizing tickets by type gives a genuine axis to compare resolution durations. Values track short_description well (WiFi->connectivity, database->database, printing->printer). Partly redundant with existing 'category' column but the derived text-based categorization adds leverage.

per_column.name: infrastructure_component
per_column.rationale: A finer-grained component axis (vpn, wifi, database) that is soundly extracted from short_description. Overlaps substantially with incident_category but adds some finer detail useful for duration comparison.

per_column.name: assigned_technician
per_column.rationale: Technician identity is a plausible driver of duration variation, but values appear derived from closed_by (already present) and several samples contradict the source: closed_by 'Charlie Whitherspoon' -> beth_anglin, closed_by 'Luke Wilson' -> charlie_whitherspoon. Mismatches suggest fabricated/misaligned assignment; largely redundant with existing assigned_to/closed_by columns.

per_column.name: problem_scope
per_column.rationale: Scope (individual vs system-wide) is a strong potential explanatory axis for duration. However the source text rarely states scope; 'Cannot connect to office VPN' -> system_wide vs single_location inconsistently across near-identical rows, indicating unwarranted specificity/invention beyond what text supports.

per_column.name: issue_complexity_signal
per_column.rationale: Complexity is highly relevant to resolution duration. But labels like 'access_escalation' for 'Cannot connect to office WiFi' are not supported by the terse descriptions; the mapping asserts specifics the text does not establish, indicating inference beyond the source.

per_column.name: caller_recurrence_status
per_column.rationale: Recurrence could plausibly relate to duration and is in principle derivable by aggregating caller_id across rows, so partly grounded. Sample rows lack caller_id evidence to verify, and the high/low frequency distinction is not clearly justified, lowering confidence.

per_column.name: self_closure_indicator
per_column.rationale: Whether a ticket was self-closed could correlate with duration. Derivable in principle by comparing closed_by to caller_id, but samples show no caller_id to confirm the True/False values, so groundedness is uncertain; also somewhat generic binary flag.

per_column.name: temporal_shift_indicator
per_column.rationale: Time-of-day shift is a well-grounded derivation from opened_at and a plausible driver of resolution speed. Some boundary labels are questionable (8:50 -> business_hours ok; 17:40 -> after_hours vs 18:14 -> after_hours reasonable), overall soundly derived from timestamps.

judge.rationale: Most columns provide genuine new axes (category, component, scope, complexity, shift) to explain duration variation, so table-level usefulness is solid despite some redundancy among the category/component pair and with existing columns. Groundedness is mixed: text-extraction columns (incident_category, infrastructure_component, temporal_shift_indicator) are well supported, but assigned_technician contradicts closed_by in multiple samples, and problem_scope and issue_complexity_signal assert specifics the terse descriptions do not warrant, showing hallucination.
